newsitem.title: USA: U.S. poultry groups blast EU meat trade pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. poultry groups blast EU meat trade pact.

text.p: U.S. poultry groups on Wednesday criticized a trade pact reached between the United States and European Union officials as an action that will "slam the door shut" for imports of U.S. poultry.

"The unreasonable and unyielding stance of the European Union during trade talks is nothing more than a blatant attempt to restrict competition from U.S. poultry companies in Europe," said a statement issued by the National Broiler Council, the National Turkey Federation and the USA Poultry and Egg Export Council.
The U.S. poultry industry stands to lose $34.2 million in broiler trade with the EU, plus $10 million in turkeys and $8 million in spent hens, the groups said.

Earlier Wednesday afternoon, U.S. agriculture negotiator Paul Drazek told reporters that U.S. poultry exports to Europe would remain halted. On April 1, the EU imposed new rules halting U.S. poultry shipments to Europe.

Negotiators reached a last-minute agreement in the so-called "veterinary equivalency" talks, averting a costly trade war in which Washington had threatened to halt some $300 million worth of meat shipments from Europe. But the deal reached on meat trade issues did not include poultry, Drazek said.
"European chicken and turkey producers have been protected from American competition since the early 1960s, and the protectionism has triumphed once again," the poultry groups said in the statement.

At issue in the talks was whether the two sides, which use different meat inspection procedures, could agree on a method for determining that each other's products were safe. The EU objected to the U.S. poultry industry's use of chlorinated water and anti-microbial agents to decontaminate poultry carcasses.
Talks have been underway between the EU and U.S. officials for three years to recognize inspection and sanitary procedures.
